newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won closes at six-year low on yen's fall.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won closes at six-year low on yen's fall.

text.p: The won closed Wednesday trading at a new six-year low affected by the Japanese yen's drop against the U.S. unit and dollar short-covering by banks, dealers said.
The won opened the day's trading at 853.00 and closed at 854.50, the lowest level since the market-average system was introduced in March 1990.
It touched an intraday high of 852.50 in the morning after the central bank intervened, selling dollars to stop the won's drop, dealers said. The Bank of Korea denied intervening.
"The won will remain weak unless there is a big change in economic fundamentals," said a foreign bank dealer.
In Tokyo, the dollar rose to a 46-month high of 118.75 yen, compared with a level of around 117.91 on Tuesday.
Dealers said the won has been under steady downward pressure as import settlements continue to outweigh exporter demand in line with a slump in exports.
They forecast the won's base mid-rate for Thursday at 853.60, compared with 852.10 on Wednesday.
